changes.old: the daughters of the inhabitants of the city
changes.new: the daughters of the men of the city
changes.hebrew_basis: ובנות אנשי העיר — 'daughters of the men of the city'; Greek τῶν οἰκούντων 'of those inhabiting'
טבת מראה מאד — mar'eh 'appearance' (column renders mar'eh 'appearance' at 29:17); 'of face' follows Greek ὄψει

changes.old: water was provided for his feet
changes.new: water was provided to wash his feet
changes.hebrew_basis: ומים לרחץ רגליו — 'water to wash his feet'; לרחץ omitted
לדבר אל־לבי — 'speaking to/in my heart'; Greek ἐν τῇ διανοίᾳ 'in my mind'

changes.old: because his hunting was food for him
changes.new: because game was in his mouth
changes.hebrew_basis: כי־ציד בפיו — 'for game was in his mouth'; Greek ἡ θήρα αὐτοῦ βρῶσις αὐτῷ 'his game was food for him'

changes.old: Is she then truly your wife? Why did you say
changes.new: Behold, she is surely your wife! How could you say
changes.hebrew_basis: אך הנה אשתך הוא ואיך אמרת — a statement 'surely she is your wife; and how did you say'; Greek Ἆρά γε...; τί ὅτι 'Is she then...? Why'
את־כל־העם — 'all the people'; Greek adds αὐτοῦ 'his'
וצא השדה — sadeh 'field'; Greek πεδίον 'plain'

changes.old: the bare parts of his neck
changes.new: the smooth part of his neck
changes.hebrew_basis: חלקת צואריו — chelqah 'smooth part' (cf. איש חלק 27:11); Greek τὰ γυμνά 'the bare parts'
ואת־הלחם — singular 'the bread'; Greek τοὺς ἄρτους 'the loaves'
באר בשדה — sadeh 'field'; Greek πεδίον 'plain'

changes.old: You are of my bones and of my flesh
changes.new: Surely you are my bone and my flesh
changes.hebrew_basis: אך עצמי ובשרי אתה — 'surely you are my bone and my flesh'; Greek Ἐκ τῶν ὀστῶν μου καὶ ἐκ τῆς σαρκός μου 'of my bones and of my flesh', and אך omitted

changes.old: and Jacob went in to her
changes.new: and he went in to her
changes.hebrew_basis: ויבא אליה — 'and he went in to her'; Greek repeats the name (εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὴν Ιακωβ); 'Jacob' already supplied earlier in the verse
הֵן לוּ יְהִי כִדְבָרֶךָ — הֵן ('behold/very well') omitted; English matches Greek Ἔστω κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου exactly

changes.new: “It is in the power of my hand
changes.hebrew_basis: יֶשׁ־לְאֵל יָדִי 'it is in the power of my hand' — MT has no 'and now'; Greek καὶ νῦν ἰσχύει ἡ χείρ μου
עַד עֲלוֹת הַשָּׁחַר 'until the rising of the dawn' (cf. 32:26 'the dawn has risen'); Greek ἕως πρωΐ 'until morning'
אֶת־הַשְּׁפָחוֹת — no numeral (contrast 33:1 שְׁתֵּי הַשְּׁפָחוֹת); 'two' follows Greek τὰς δύο παιδίσκας
וְאַחַר 'and afterward'; 'after these things' = Greek μετὰ ταῦτα
מַצֶּבֶת קְבֻרַת־רָחֵל 'pillar of Rachel's grave'; 'monument' = Greek μνημείου
וַיִּהְיוּ יְמֵי יִצְחָק 'the days of Isaac were' — 'in which he lived' = Greek plus ἃς ἔζησεν

changes.old: because of the multitude of their livestock
changes.hebrew_basis: מִפְּנֵי מִקְנֵיהֶם 'because of their livestock'; 'multitude' = Greek ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους

changes.old: his father loved him more than all his sons
changes.new: their father loved him more than all his brothers
changes.hebrew_basis: אֹתוֹ אָהַב אֲבִיהֶם מִכָּל־אֶחָיו 'their father loved him more than all his brothers'; Greek ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ... ἐκ πάντων τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ
תֹעֶה בַּשָּׂדֶה — sadeh 'field'; Greek ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ 'plain'
לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִים 'to the Ishmaelites'; 'these' = Greek τοῖς Ισμαηλίταις τούτοις
וַיֵּט עַד־אִישׁ עֲדֻלָּמִי 'turned aside to an Adullamite man'; Greek ἀφίκετο ἕως 'arrived as far as'
עלתה נצה — 'its blossoms came up'; Greek 'put forth shoots' (blastous)
על כף פרעה — singular 'palm/hand' (cf. 40:21); Greek plural 'into the hands'

changes.old: it seemed to me that I stood
changes.hebrew_basis: הנני עמד — 'behold, I was standing'; Greek ōmēn 'I thought/it seemed'

changes.old: the seven ugly, thin cows ate up the first seven good, fat cows
changes.new: the ugly, thin cows ate up the first seven fat cows
changes.hebrew_basis: הפרות הרקות והרעות … שבע הפרות הראשנות הבריאת — no 'seven' for the lean cows and no 'good'; both from Greek
ולא תכרת הארץ — 'the land will not be cut off'; Greek exolethreuthēsetai
וייטב הדבר — 'the thing was good' (singular); Greek 'the words were pleasing'

changes.old: in which there was abundance in the land of Egypt
changes.new: which were in the land of Egypt
changes.hebrew_basis: אשר היו בארץ מצרים — 'which were in the land of Egypt'; 'there was abundance' is the Greek (en hois ēn hē euthēnia)
שדה העיר — sadeh 'field'; Greek pedion 'plain'
ויצא לבם — 'their heart went out/failed'; Greek exestē hē kardia 'heart was astonished'
והרעב כבד בארץ — 'the famine was heavy/severe in the land' (cf. 41:31 'severe'); Greek enischysen 'prevailed'
על פי הדברים האלה — 'according to these words'; Greek kata tēn eperōtēsin 'according to this questioning'

changes.old: go down again to the man
changes.hebrew_basis: קומו שובו אל האיש — 'arise, return to the man'; Greek katabēte 'go down'

changes.old: in the gateway of the house
changes.new: in the doorway of the house
changes.hebrew_basis: פתח הבית — 'the opening/doorway of the house'; Greek pylōn 'gateway'

changes.old: with their faces to the ground
changes.hebrew_basis: וישתחוו לו ארצה — only 'to the ground' (contrast 42:6 אפים ארצה); Greek adds epi prosōpon 'on their faces'

changes.old: And he questioned them, saying, “How are you?” And he said to them, “Is your father healthy,
changes.new: And he asked them about their welfare, and said, “Is your father well,
changes.hebrew_basis: וישאל להם לשלום ויאמר השלום אביכם — 'he asked them about their welfare and said, Is your father well'; 'How are you?' and 'healthy' (hygiainei) are Greek
אשר ימצא אתו — 'with whom it is found'; Greek supplies to kondy 'the cup'

changes.old: lord of all the land of Egypt
changes.hebrew_basis: לאדון לכל מצרים — 'lord of all Egypt'; Greek pasēs gēs Aigyptou adds 'land'

changes.old: all Egypt’s good things will be yours
changes.new: the best of all the land of Egypt is yours
changes.hebrew_basis: כי טוב כל ארץ מצרים לכם הוא — 'the best of all the land of Egypt is yours'; Greek ta panta agatha Aigyptou 'all the good things of Egypt'
ויאמר פרעה אל אחיו — 'to his brothers'; Greek tois adelphois Iōsēph supplies the name
את כל הרעה — singular 'all the evil'; Greek plural panta ta kaka

note: Close reading of the 652 Genesis readings that shared the Greek column wording, against the Westminster Leningrad Codex. Applied with the Arpachshad name form (10:22, 10:24, 11:10–13) and 41:57 "all the earth".
